name: Red
desc: The one you picked, tidied: Archivo, black rules, signal red. The back splits red and black on the diagonal.

name: Blue squares
desc: Same grid in ultramarine. The back is a set of nested squares, like a target seen from above.

name: Exam paper
desc: Inspired by the IB exam room: ruled answer lines, candidate-number boxes and an ink-blue accent.

name: Seven
desc: Seven is the top IB grade, so the back is one big outlined 7. Green accent, Hanken Grotesk.

name: Night
desc: The grid inverted: pure black, white rules, red for your turn. Backs are fine white hatching.

name: Dots
desc: Yellow highlighter on black and white. The back is a black card with a grid of yellow dots.

name: Tall
desc: Condensed display type for huge numerals in little space. Backs are a tight run of vertical stripes.

name: Forty-five
desc: A nod to the 45-point diploma: each back carries a round 45 seal. Orange-red and Bricolage Grotesque.

name: Ledger
desc: Everything sits in cells, like a results table. Hairline grid, checkerboard backs, Familjen Grotesk.

name: Flip
desc: The name made literal: each back shows an F and its mirror image. Black, white and one green.

name: Quiet felt
desc: A flat green table with nothing extra: no rail, no glow, plain white cards.

name: Notepad
desc: Blue ballpoint on graph paper, like a scorepad on the kitchen table.

name: Navy and brass
desc: A members' card room: deep navy, ivory cards, brass details.

name: Lilac pop
desc: A chunky, friendly mobile game: thick outlines, solid shadows, big tap targets.

name: Swiss
desc: No table at all. A strict grid of rows, one red, giant numerals.

name: Game night
desc: A 1970s board-game box: mustard, brown and orange, striped card backs.

name: Pocket
desc: A four-shade handheld screen with pixel type and hard edges.

name: Indigo
desc: Indigo-dyed cloth and pale paper, with wave-patterned card backs.

name: Big numbers
desc: Cards reduced to one huge numeral each, readable from across the room.

name: Picnic
desc: Daylight: a blue gingham cloth, soft paper cards, rounded everything.
